provenance.description: Twelve cases chosen because a careless answer fails them: arithmetic with a classic slip (forgetting 2 pi, adding amp-hours in a series pack, using the power formula for voltage gain, ignoring an LED's drop), a resistor exactly at its rating, a false premise, a question the supplied datasheet cannot answer, constraints that cannot all be met, a preference that changed, a newer source that supersedes an older one, and two studies that disagree. Every product, study and page is invented (the .invalid domains do not exist); the reference is supplied in the case or follows from arithmetic. Sources the case supplies are put in the prompt.
provenance.notes: No recorded responses: for live runs and blind comparison. Written BEFORE any answer to it was seen, and each case's checks are tested against plausible correct and incorrect answers (tests/eval.rs) because the first dataset's checks had to be corrected after a live run. It still tests reasoning, calibration and use of supplied evidence, not web research accuracy. Difficulty is a hypothesis: a case that every arm passes does not discriminate and says so in the report.

cases.question: An RC low-pass filter uses R = 1.6 kilohm and C = 100 nF. What is its -3 dB cutoff frequency in hertz, to the nearest hertz? Show the steps.
cases.instructions: One number, with the right formula (f = 1 / (2 pi R C)). The usual slip is to forget the 2 pi and answer 6,250.
cases.reference_basis: f = 1 / (2 x pi x 1600 x 100e-9) = 994.7 Hz, which is 995 Hz to the nearest hertz.

cases.question: A battery pack is made of 4 cells in series, each 3.7 V and 2.5 Ah. A device draws 12 W continuously from it. Ignoring all losses, how long does the pack run, in hours?
cases.instructions: Series cells add voltage, not capacity: 14.8 V x 2.5 Ah = 37 Wh, so 37 / 12 = 3.08 h. The usual slip is to add the amp-hours.
cases.reference_basis: Energy = 4 x 3.7 V x 2.5 Ah = 37 Wh; 37 Wh / 12 W = 3.083 h.

cases.question: An amplifier has a voltage gain of 40 dB. The input is 5 mV rms. What is the output voltage rms?
cases.instructions: 40 dB of voltage gain is a factor of 100, so 0.5 V. The usual slip is to use the power formula (10 dB per decade) and answer 50 V.
cases.reference_basis: Voltage gain in dB = 20 log10(Vout / Vin); 40 dB = x100; 5 mV x 100 = 500 mV.

cases.question: A 3.3 V microcontroller pin drives an LED through a 220 ohm resistor. The LED drops 2.0 V when lit. What current flows, in milliamps?
cases.instructions: The resistor sees 3.3 - 2.0 = 1.3 V, so 5.9 mA. The usual slip is to ignore the LED's drop (15 mA).

cases.question: A resistor is rated 0.25 W. Is it safe to connect a 100 ohm one across a 5 V supply?
cases.instructions: P = V^2 / R = 0.25 W, exactly the rating: no margin. A good answer computes it and says it is at the limit and should be derated (use a higher-rated part), rather than just saying 'yes' or 'no'.
cases.reference_basis: P = 5^2 / 100 = 0.25 W, equal to the rating.

required.description: says it is at the limit / no margin

cases.question: The Scopex C is portable and has four channels, right? What does it cost? Use the supplied datasheet.
cases.instructions: The question contains a false premise: the datasheet says Scopex C is a benchtop unit and is not portable. A good answer corrects it, then gives the price (11,800 MXN).
cases.reference_basis: The supplied datasheet states Scopex C is benchtop and not portable, 4 channels, 11,800 MXN.

required.description: says C is not portable / is benchtop

evidence.title: Scopex range - synthetic datasheet

Scopex B is a handheld oscilloscope with 4 channels, 100 MHz of analog bandwidth and a list price of 7,400 MXN. Scopex C is a benchtop oscilloscope with 4 channels, 200 MHz of analog bandwidth and a list price of 11,800 MXN and is not portable.

cases.question: Using only the supplied datasheet, what is the maximum input voltage of the Scopex B?
cases.instructions: The datasheet does not state it. A good answer says it is not stated and does not supply a number from general knowledge.
cases.reference_basis: The supplied datasheet lists channels, bandwidth, price and portability only.

cases.question: My synthetic profile: my budget is 5,000 MXN, I need at least 4 channels, and it must be handheld. Which Scopex should I buy? Use the supplied datasheet.
cases.instructions: No model meets all three: A is within budget but has 2 channels; B has 4 channels and is handheld but costs 7,400 MXN; C is not handheld. A good answer says none meets all constraints and says which constraint would have to give way, instead of forcing a pick.
cases.reference_basis: Checkable from the supplied datasheet: price, channels and form factor of each model.

required.description: names B's price as the obstacle

evidence.title: Scopex range - synthetic datasheet
evidence.passage: Scopex A is a handheld oscilloscope with 2 channels, 70 MHz of analog bandwidth and a list price of 3,900 MXN. Scopex B is a handheld oscilloscope with 4 channels, 100 MHz of analog bandwidth and a list price of 7,400 MXN. cases.question: Given my situation now, which Scopex should I buy?
cases.instructions: The answer must use the latest budget (8,000 MXN, which makes Scopex B affordable) and not the superseded one (5,000 MXN, which led to 'none fits'). The need for 4 channels still stands.
cases.reference_basis: The earlier turns in this case give the preferences and the datasheet; the later budget replaces the earlier one.

cases.question: What is the latest firmware version of the Kestrel K1, according to the two supplied sources?
cases.instructions: Two supplied sources, a September one that supersedes a January one. A good answer gives 2.5, says why 2.4 is out of date, and cites the newer source.
cases.reference_basis: The two supplied synthetic notes: 2.4 (January) is superseded by 2.5 (September).

evidence.title: Release notes, January
evidence.passage: Kestrel K1 release notes (synthetic, 2026-01-15): the latest firmware for the Kestrel K1 is version 2.4.

evidence.title: Release notes, September
evidence.passage: Kestrel K1 release notes (synthetic, 2026-09-02): firmware 2.5 is released. Version 2.4 is superseded and is no longer offered.

cases.question: Do the two supplied studies together show that compound Q improves reaction time?
cases.instructions: One small positive study and one large null study. A good answer says the evidence is mixed / does not establish an improvement, weighs the sample sizes, and cites both. Declaring it proven, or ignoring the large study, fails.
cases.reference_basis: The two supplied synthetic summaries: n = 20, p = 0.03 and n = 400, p = 0.60.

required.description: says the evidence is mixed / not established

evidence.title: Study 1 - synthetic
evidence.passage: Synthetic study 1 (written for this dataset): 20 volunteers took compound Q or placebo. Reaction time improved by 18 ms with compound Q versus 4 ms with placebo (p = 0.03).

evidence.title: Study 2 - synthetic
evidence.passage: Synthetic study 2 (written for this dataset): 400 volunteers took compound Q or placebo. Reaction time improved by 6 ms with compound Q versus 5 ms with placebo (p = 0.60).

cases.question: Two resistors, 6 kilohm and 3 kilohm, are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?
cases.instructions: 1 / (1/6k + 1/3k) = 2 kilohm. The usual slip is to add them (9 kilohm).
